sessions.title: Pelvic Floor Anatomy & Levels of Support

objectiveGroups.heading: Anatomy (GTL 1a-j)
objectives: Demonstrate knowledge of pelvic anatomy: genital, urinary, colorectal, musculoskeletal elements
Describe vascular supply to pelvic organs (external genitalia, uterus, kidney, ureter, urethra, bladder, anus, rectosigmoid)
Describe nerve supply to pelvic organs (sympathetic, parasympathetic, somatic, pelvic autonomic plexuses)
Explain normal anatomic supports of vagina, rectum, bladder, urethra, and uterus
Describe pelvic/retroperitoneal spaces; anterior abdominal wall anatomy
Describe vascular and nerve supply to urethral and anal sphincter mechanisms

objectiveGroups.heading: Embryology (GTL 1i-j)
objectives: Describe normal embryologic development of genital and urinary tract
Describe common congenital abnormalities vs normal anatomy

sessions.reading: Walters Ch. 1: Anatomy of the lower urinary tract, pelvic floor, and rectum

sessions.title: Lower Urinary Tract Function & Continence Mechanisms

objectiveGroups.heading: LUT Physiology (GTL 2a)
objectives: Describe normal LUT function during storage and micturition; continence mechanisms
Role of CNS, spinal, supraspinal, and PNS on LUT function
Reflex pathways: sympathetic, parasympathetic, somatic interactions
Key neurotransmitters: adrenergic, cholinergic, NO, ATP, growth factors
Urethral sphincter mechanism at rest and with physical stress
Pharmacologic agents for LUTD: anticholinergics, beta-3 agonists, alpha blockers
Estrogen and progesterone effects on GU tract function

objectiveGroups.heading: Colorectal & Utero-vaginal Physiology (GTL 2b-c)
objectives: Colorectal function physiology; dietary and pharmacologic influences
Normal uterine/vaginal function before and after menopause

sessions.title: SUI: Comprehensive Evaluation & Treatment

objectiveGroups.heading: Evaluation (GTL UI&LUTS; 3a)
objectives: Directed history: UI/LUTS symptoms, type, duration, severity, contributing factors
Screen for co-existing PFDs; evaluate environmental factors/diseases impacting treatment
Impact of medications on UI/LUTS (sedatives, hypnotics, diuretics, antidepressants)
Focused pelvic floor exam: stress testing, urethral mobility, PVR, muscle tone, reflexes, neuro status

objectiveGroups.heading: Non-Surgical Treatment (GTL UI&LUTS; 4a-e)
objectives: Functional interventions: weight optimization, fluid management, toileting, ISC, pads
PFPT: muscle strength building, relaxation, trigger point management
Pharmacologic: anti-muscarinics, beta-agonists, topical estrogen, TCAs, SNRIs
Pessaries for UI/LUTS: types, fitting, care, complications, compliance

objectiveGroups.heading: Surgical Treatment (GTL UI&LUTS; 5b-h)
objectives: Retropubic and transobturator MUS, mini-slings; fascial/pubovaginal slings
Urethral bulking agents; Burch urethropexy/colposuspension
For all: indications, contraindications, success rates, complications, patient selection
Mesh and graft use in surgical procedures for UI/LUTS

sessions.title: Research Methodology & Study Design

objectiveGroups.heading: Study Design (GTL Scholarly Activity 1-7)
objectives: Design hypothesis-driven study: problem, hypothesis, specific aims, significance, sample size
Study bias (selection, information, confounding); study design types
Measures of central tendency; parametric vs non-parametric analysis
Prevalence vs incidence; sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV
Power analysis; Type I and Type II error
Statistical tests: chi-square, t-test, Mann-Whitney U, ANOVA, regression, survival analysis
Interpret confidence intervals and research limitations
